sentences.text: Shri Vivek Singh, learned counsel for the appellant.

Shri Sachin Jaiswal, learned Panel Lawyer for the respon I.A. No. 3553/2024, an application for urgent hearing is taken up and hereby disposed of.
2.
Heard on I.A. No. 3551/2024, which is an application filed under Section 389 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for suspension of sentence filed on behalf of appellant No. 1 Arvind.

3. The appellant has been convicted for offence under Sections 376 (2)
(n), 363 and 366(A) of I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo 10 years R.I., 02 years R.I. and 02 years R.I.
with fine of Rs.2,000/-, Rs.200/- and Rs.200/- respectively and with default stipulations.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
There are material contradictions and omissions in the statements of the witnesses.
He has further submitted that the prosecutrix and present appellant have lived together for approximately three years and eight months, two children were also born.
Now, the prosecutrix has married with someone and both children are residing their step-father.

He has also submitted that in this case the appellant has completed incarceration period of 4 years 11 months and 16 days out of 10 years and he is ready to take the custody of both children, if the prosecutrix handed over them.
There is no likelihood of final hearing of this appeal.

Hence,
remaining jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended.
5. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.

6. Considering the custody period of the appellant and other facts and circumstances of the case,
without commenting on the merits of the case, I deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant because final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
7. Consequently, I.A.No.3551/2024 is allowed.
The execution of jail sentence of appellant No. 1 Arvind is hereby suspended subject to depositing the fine amount, (if not already deposited).

It is Arvind vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49638504/
1 directed that the appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond to a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 20.08.2024 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Regisry in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
